action.description: Dummy root holding the kernel world model and initial branch alternatives.
action.rationale: No implementation is attached to the root; real implementation choices begin in child nodes.
action.title: World model root

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc Pro B70/XPU Triton target; fixed fp16 C=32, window N=16, hidden=128 are favorable for small-tile kernels but not necessarily for large vendor GEMM paths.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The total work is dominated by dense linear layers, while the attention core is many independent small 16x16 softmax-attention problems.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Actual tl.dot throughput and preferred tile shapes on Intel XPU backend are unknown.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Reference materializes multiple full-size tensors and window reshapes; a custom path can reduce global traffic by fusing layernorm, projections, attention, MLP, and residuals.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Weights are small enough for cache, but repeated per-window loads and intermediate spills may still dominate if fusion is too register-heavy.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window state includes 16x32 activations, q/k/v, 16x16 logits/probabilities, and MLP hidden tiles; full fusion is possible but tight.
register_pressure.risk: Over-fused kernels may spill or reduce occupancy on XPU, erasing bandwidth savings.

nodes.notes:
1) Classification: mixed dense per-token reductions, matrix-multiply-like projections, small-window attention/softmax, GELU elementwise, residual adds; outputs are NHWC fp16 same shape as input; access is dense, no sparse indirection if windows are mapped directly from NHWC. Fixed dims: B=1, H=720, W=1280, C=32, Wh=Ww=4, N=16, heads=1, hidden=128, windows=57600.
2) Canonical math: y0=LN1(x) over C; q,k,v = affine_C_to_3C(y0); for each 4x4 window, A=softmax((q/sqrt(C)) k^T + rpe) over N; attn_out=proj(A v); x1=x+attn_out; y1=LN2(x1); mlp=fc2(GELU(fc1(y1))); out=x1+mlp. Independent windows for attention; independent tokens for LN/MLP; reductions are C=32, N=16, hidden=128. Stable fp32 accumulation is needed for LN, softmax, and dot reductions.
3) Layout/access: x/out are contiguous NHWC fp16, token channel vectors contiguous; window rows are dense channel vectors with row stride W*C. Weights: norm gamma/beta 32 each, qkv weight 96x32, proj 32x32, fc1 128x32, fc2 32x128, biases contiguous fp16; rpe 16x16 fp16/fp32 buffer. Dominant traffic in eager comes from intermediate tensors qkv, attn, proj, fc1 hidden, and LN outputs. Small weights can be cached; activations benefit from staying in registers/local memory within a window or token tile.
4) Bottleneck regimes: Regime A eager/compiled baseline is launch/intermediate-memory dominated due many ops and large tensors. Regime B custom staged dense GEMM is compute-throughput dominated by qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 but pays global writes. Regime C monolithic window fusion is register/occupancy limited if it keeps too much state. Regime D minimal attention-only optimization is softmax latency and small-matrix overhead dominated, with limited overall speedup because MLP/projections dominate FLOPs.
5) Design knobs: granularity per window vs token block vs staged matrix tiles; whether to materialize qkv/hidden; C and hidden tiling; fp32 vs fp16 accumulation points; exact GELU implementation; softmax stability; mapping NHWC windows directly vs contiguous scratch; number of rows/windows per program; cache strategy for small weights/rpe; residual/LN fusion boundaries.
6) Skeleton: load input tile/window, compute LN1 mean/variance in fp32, apply affine norm, compute q/k/v, form 16x16 logits with rpe and stable row softmax, multiply by v, apply proj and residual to get x1, compute LN2, run fc1/GELU/fc2 in hidden tiles, add residual and store. Synchronization should only be program-local; global synchronization is unnecessary.
7) Candidate families pruned: end-to-end window-block path minimizes memory but risks spills; staged dense-transform path is robust and more GEMM-like but writes intermediates; feed-forward-dominant path is lowest-risk and targets the largest MLP cost but leaves attention/reference overhead.

action.description: Implement a first ModelNew prototype that computes the entire fixed-shape Swin block through a window-local Triton path, avoiding materialized qkv, attention, LN, and MLP intermediates where practical.
action.rationale: The reference performs many memory-bound framework operations over 921600 tokens. A direct window-local path can cut global traffic to mostly input/output plus weights, which should be a large win if register pressure stays controlled.
action.title: End-to-end window-block path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Fixed N=16 and C=32 fit naturally into small Triton tiles; hidden=128 may need inner tiling to avoid excessive state.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: High arithmetic reuse per loaded activation and small weights; best potential if tl.dot maps well for many small reductions.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: A monolithic program may be too small for peak matrix throughput or too large in registers for good occupancy.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Best-case memory behavior: read x once, write out once, reuse weights from cache, and avoid full-size qkv/LN/hidden tensors.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Spills or repeated weight loads per window could reduce the expected bandwidth advantage.

register_pressure.notes: Needs to hold or stream 16 token channel vectors, q/k/v fragments, softmax rows, and MLP hidden fragments.
register_pressure.risk: Most serious risk; full fusion may force spills or require multiple passes over activations.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This sibling is an alternative first implementation because it commits to one fused window-resident execution model; it cannot be combined in the same first iteration with staged or MLP-only paths without changing the core code structure and measurement target. Intended for the memory-traffic-dominated regime where eliminating intermediates matters more than using large GEMM-like tiles. Primary limiter is register pressure and XPU occupancy.

action.description: Implement a staged custom Triton pipeline with natural boundaries around LN+qkv, window attention+proj, LN+fc1+GELU, and fc2+residual, using explicit intermediate tensors.
action.rationale: This preserves numerical structure and reduces framework overhead while keeping each kernel moderate in register use and easier to validate.
action.title: Staged block pipeline path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Dense linear stages can be mapped as large collections of fixed C=32/H=128 dot products; attention stage remains small N=16.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: More likely to achieve stable compilation and decent arithmetic utilization than a monolithic kernel.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small reduction dimensions may still underutilize hardware compared with large GEMMs.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Writes qkv, projected attention, and MLP hidden or partials unless further fused; still better than eager if kernels combine adjacent operations.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Intermediate tensor traffic could become the dominant cost, especially fc1 hidden of shape 921600x128.

register_pressure.notes: Each stage has bounded live state; attention and MLP can tile independently.
register_pressure.risk: Moderate pressure in attention softmax and hidden tiling, but much lower than full fusion.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This sibling is mutually exclusive as a first implementation with end-to-end fusion because it deliberately materializes intermediates to reduce risk; it is also different from MLP-only because all block stages are owned by custom kernels from the start. Intended for a balanced compute/memory regime. Primary limiter is intermediate global memory traffic.

action.description: Implement a targeted Triton replacement for the norm2 plus fc1/GELU/fc2 residual feed-forward portion, while initially keeping the attention path close to the reference for correctness and faster iteration.
action.rationale: The MLP is a major FLOP contributor and has simple dense per-token dependencies, making it a low-risk first speedup and correctness baseline.
action.title: Feed-forward-dominant path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Per-token C=32 to hidden=128 to C=32 is regular and fixed; can process many tokens per program without window coupling.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Good fit for dense dot-product style kernels; avoids the more fragile window attention softmax initially.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If PyTorch attention remains in the path, launch and memory overhead outside the MLP may cap total speedup.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Can fuse LN2, fc1, GELU, fc2, and residual to avoid storing the 921600x128 hidden tensor.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Still reads and writes the full activation after attention; no savings in qkv/attention intermediates.

register_pressure.notes: Hidden dimension can be streamed or tiled; no need to hold window attention matrices.
register_pressure.risk: Holding too many hidden channels per token may still reduce occupancy, but it is manageable.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This sibling is an alternative first implementation because it intentionally optimizes only the feed-forward half for rapid validation; combining it immediately with full attention ownership would become the staged-pipeline sibling. Intended for low-risk early speedup. Primary limiter is unoptimized attention/reference overhead.

action.description: Implement a custom Triton path focused on window partition-free attention, including norm1, qkv, 16x16 softmax attention, projection, and first residual, while leaving the MLP path conventional initially.
action.rationale: The attention path has many small-window operations and layout transforms that eager PyTorch handles poorly; optimizing it first isolates the unique Swin-window bottleneck.
action.title: Window-attention-dominant path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: N=16 softmax rows and C=32 q/k/v reductions are small; best if many windows are processed efficiently across XPU execution units.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Targets the most layout-sensitive part and avoids materializing window-partitioned tensors.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Attention is not the largest FLOP share, so total speedup may be modest even if this part is much faster.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Can avoid qkv and attention materialization and write only x1, but still leaves MLP intermediates to the remaining path.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If MLP remains memory-heavy, attention savings may be hidden in end-to-end timing.

register_pressure.notes: Must retain q/k/v fragments and 16x16 logits/probabilities, but avoids MLP hidden state.
register_pressure.risk: Softmax plus qkv/proj in one kernel could still be register intensive.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This sibling is an alternative first implementation because it prioritizes Swin-specific window attention and defers feed-forward optimization; combining both immediately would be the end-to-end or staged block sibling. Intended for regimes where window partition, softmax, and small attention launches dominate observed latency. Primary limiter is limited overall FLOP coverage.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape simplified Swin block over NHWC fp16 input [1,720,1280,32] with 57600 independent 4x4 windows, single-head N=16 attention, two C=32 layernorm reductions, dense projections qkv/proj, and a C=32->128->32 GELU MLP. The main optimization opportunity is to avoid PyTorch eager/compiled overhead and large intermediate tensors by exploiting fixed small dimensions and direct NHWC window mapping; the main risks are fp32 numerical matching for LayerNorm/softmax/GELU on Intel XPU Triton and register pressure when fusing attention plus MLP. Likely bottlenecks shift from framework/intermediate-memory bandwidth in the reference to small-tile dot throughput, cache reuse of small weights, and occupancy/spilling in custom kernels.
open_questions: What correctness tolerance does the evaluator use for fp16 outputs, especially for LayerNorm accumulation, softmax, and exact versus approximate GELU?
Does the Intel XPU Triton backend support all needed primitives reliably for this task, including tl.dot on fp16, tl.exp, tl.erf, and efficient masked loads/stores?
Are input shape, dim=32, window_size=4x4, batch=1, and H/W exactly fixed in all tests, or must ModelNew handle nearby dynamic shapes?
Is benchmark timing inclusive of first-call Triton compilation, parameter copying, or one-time buffer allocation, or only steady-state forward latency?
How fast are PyTorch eager and torch.compile baselines on Arc Pro B70 for this exact model, and which reference substage dominates measured latency?
Will the evaluator load arbitrary trained weights, requiring exact handling of all state_dict parameters including norm weights/biases and rpe_bias dtype/layout?
What are the practical register, occupancy, and local-memory limits for Triton programs on Arc Pro B70 for window-sized attention plus tiled MLP?
